steps.name: environment - create venv, prepare logs, optional persistent headless flag
steps.description: Prepare the workspace and logs, ensure python3-venv is present, create an idempotent virtualenv at $WS/.venv using system python3, and verify the venv python and pip. Upgrade pip inside the venv using the venv's absolute python. Export STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true for the current session. Optionally persist STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS globally to /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh when STREAMLIT_PERSIST_ENV=true. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp and is non-interactive and idempotent.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp"
mkdir -p "$WS" "$WS/logs" && cd "$WS"
# Ensure system venv support
if ! python3 -m venv --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null && sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q python3-venv >/dev/null
fi
# Create venv idempotently
if [ ! -d "$WS/.venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$WS/.venv"
fi
VENV_PY="$WS/.venv/bin/python"
# Validate venv python exists
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "error: venv python not found at $VENV_PY" >&2
  exit 5
fi
# Upgrade pip inside venv
mkdir -p "$WS/logs"
"$VENV_PY" -m pip install --upgrade pip >"$WS/logs/pip_upgrade_env.log" 2>&1 || { cat "$WS/logs/pip_upgrade_env.log" >&2; exit 10; }
# Export headless for current session
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true
# Optional persistent global export (controlled by STREAMLIT_PERSIST_ENV); default off
if [ "${STREAMLIT_PERSIST_ENV:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  PROFILE_FILE=/etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh
  TMPFILE=$(mktemp)
  cat > "$TMPFILE" <<'EOF'
# Streamlit automation defaults (created by setup script)
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_HEADLESS=true
# To remove: sudo rm -f /etc/profile.d/streamlit_env.sh
EOF
  sudo mv "$TMPFILE" "$PROFILE_FILE" && sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE_FILE" || { echo "failed to write $PROFILE_FILE with sudo" >&2; rm -f "$TMPFILE" || true; exit 11; }
fi
# Verify venv pip usable
"$VENV_PY" -m pip -V >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "venv pip unusable" >&2; exit 12; }

steps.name: scaffolding - create project files, pinned requirements, streamlit config, and healthcheck
steps.description: Create deterministic top-level requirements.txt (pinned), an import-safe minimal Streamlit app (app.py), .streamlit/config.toml for container defaults, a resilient healthcheck script using curl with timeouts, and a minimal pytest that imports the module. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp"
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
# Deterministic top-level requirements (pinned)
cat > "$WS/requirements.txt" <<'REQ'
streamlit==1.30.0
pandas==2.2.2
numpy==1.26.5
pytest==7.4.2
REQ
# Minimal import-safe Streamlit app
cat > "$WS/app.py" <<'PY'
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def create_ui():
    st.title('StreamlitFinanceApp - minimal')
    if st.button('show'):
        st.write(pd.DataFrame({'a': np.arange(3)}))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    create_ui()
PY
# .streamlit config
mkdir -p "$WS/.streamlit"
cat > "$WS/.streamlit/config.toml" <<'CT'
[server]
headless = true
port = 8501
enableCORS = false
CT
# Health check script
cat > "$WS/healthcheck.sh" <<'HC'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PORT=${1:-${STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT:-8501}}
ATTEMPTS=${2:-10}
SLEEP=${3:-3}
TIMEOUT_CONNECT=1
TIMEOUT_TOTAL=3
i=0
while [ $i -lt $ATTEMPTS ]; do
  if curl --connect-timeout $TIMEOUT_CONNECT --max-time $TIMEOUT_TOTAL -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
  fi
  i=$((i+1))
  sleep $SLEEP
done
exit 1
HC
chmod +x "$WS/healthcheck.sh"
# Minimal pytest that imports app
mkdir -p "$WS/tests"
cat > "$WS/tests/test_import.py" <<'PT'
def test_import_app():
    import importlib
    m = importlib.import_module('app')
    assert hasattr(m, 'create_ui') or hasattr(m, '__name__')
PT
# pytest.ini
cat > "$WS/pytest.ini" <<'PI'
[pytest]
minversion = 6.0
addopts = -q
PI
# README.setup
cat > "$WS/README.setup" <<'RD'
This workspace uses a Python venv at .venv to isolate packages from system Python. Top-level requirements are pinned; the installer will attempt to auto-adjust numpy if a pinned wheel is incompatible with the running Python.

steps.name: dependencies - install pinned python dependencies into venv with compatibility fallback for numpy
steps.description: Install pinned requirements into the workspace venv using absolute venv python. If pip fails due to an incompatible pinned numpy (no matching distribution), automatically query PyPI for the newest numpy wheel compatible with the current Python interpreter, update requirements.txt (backing up the original), and retry installation. Use --no-cache-dir and --prefer-binary to favor wheels, create logs under $WS/logs, and validate by importing streamlit and pytest. This resolves the reported CRITICAL blocking issue by performing a conservative, auditable numpy pin relaxation only when necessary. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp"
cd "$WS"
VENV_PY="$WS/.venv/bin/python"
VENV_PIP="$WS/.venv/bin/pip"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then echo "venv missing, run env-01" >&2; exit 6; fi
mkdir -p "$WS/logs"
# Ensure pip is recent
"$VENV_PY" -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel >"$WS/logs/pip_upgrade.log" 2>&1 || { cat "$WS/logs/pip_upgrade.log" >&2; exit 13; }
# Try install with retries
attempts=0
max=3
backoff=2
install_ok=0
while [ $attempts -lt $max ]; do
  if "$VENV_PY" -m pip install --prefer-binary --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt >"$WS/logs/pip_install.log" 2>&1; then
    install_ok=1 && break
  fi
  attempts=$((attempts+1))
  sleep $((backoff * attempts))
done
if [ $install_ok -eq 0 ]; then
  # Inspect logs for numpy no matching distribution
  if grep -E "No matching distribution found for numpy==|Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement numpy==" "$WS/logs/pip_install.log" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Attempt to find a compatible numpy version via pip index versions query
    # Back up original requirements
    cp requirements.txt requirements.txt.bak
    PY_VER=$("$VENV_PY" -c 'import sys; print("{}.{}".format(sys.version_info.major, sys.version_info.minor))')
    # Query simple API for available numpy versions and pick newest compatible wheel by asking pip index
    CAND=$("$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import json,sys,subprocess
req='numpy'
# use pip index versions to list available versions
try:
    out = subprocess.check_output([sys.executable,'-m','pip','index','versions',req], stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
    # pip prints lines like 'Available versions: 1.2.3, 1.2.2, ...'
    for line in out.splitlines():
        if 'Available versions:' in line:
            verstr=line.split(':',1)[1].strip()
            versions=[v.strip() for v in verstr.split(',') if v.strip()]
            if versions:
                print(versions[0])
                sys.exit(0)
except Exception:
    pass
# fallback empty
sys.exit(1)
PY
)
    if [ -n "${CAND:-}" ]; then
      # Replace numpy line in requirements.txt with the candidate
      sed -E "s/^numpy([<=>].*)?$/numpy==${CAND}/" requirements.txt.bak > requirements.txt || cp requirements.txt.bak requirements.txt
      echo "Updated requirements.txt with numpy==${CAND}" >"$WS/logs/requirements_adjust.log"
      # Retry install once
      if "$VENV_PY" -m pip install --prefer-binary --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt >"$WS/logs/pip_install_retry.log" 2>&1; then
        install_ok=1
      else
        echo "pip install still failed after numpy fallback; see logs" >&2
        tail -n 200 "$WS/logs/pip_install_retry.log" >&2 || true
        exit 14
      fi
    else
      echo "Could not determine a compatible numpy version automatically; check $WS/logs/pip_install.log" >&2
      tail -n 200 "$WS/logs/pip_install.log" >&2 || true
      exit 14
    fi
  else
    echo "pip install failed for reasons other than pinned numpy incompatibility; see logs" >&2
    tail -n 200 "$WS/logs/pip_install.log" >&2 || true
    exit 14
  fi
fi
# Validate imports
"$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import sys
try:
    import streamlit as s
    import pytest as p
    import numpy as n
    import pandas as pd
    print('python', sys.version.split()[0])
    print('streamlit', s.__version__)
    print('pytest', p.__version__)
    print('numpy', n.__version__)
    print('pandas', pd.__version__)
except Exception as e:
    print('validation import failed:', e, file=sys.stderr)
    raise
PY

steps.name: validation - start Streamlit via venv python, probe readiness (HTTP+log), and clean stop
steps.description: Start Streamlit using the venv python binary, verify the process, poll the HTTP endpoint until ready (up to 90s), run the healthcheck script, then cleanly terminate the process group. Provides logs under $WS/logs as evidence. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp and depends on all prior steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/streamlit-18635-18642/StreamlitFinanceApp"
cd "$WS"
VENV_PY="$WS/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then echo "venv missing" >&2; exit 6; fi
PORT=${STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT:-8501}
export STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT="$PORT"
LOG="$WS/logs/streamlit_validation.log"
mkdir -p "$WS/logs"
# Start streamlit via venv python in new session
setsid "$VENV_PY" -m streamlit run "$WS/app.py" --server.headless true --server.port "$PORT" >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
ST_PID=$!
sleep 1
if ! ps -p "$ST_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "streamlit process died immediately" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  exit 30
fi
# Poll HTTP endpoint up to 90s
TOTAL_TIMEOUT=90
INTERVAL=3
ELAPSED=0
READY=0
while [ $ELAPSED -lt $TOTAL_TIMEOUT ]; do
  if curl --connect-timeout 1 --max-time 3 -sSf "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    READY=1 && break
  fi
  sleep $INTERVAL
  ELAPSED=$((ELAPSED + INTERVAL))
  if ! ps -p "$ST_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "streamlit process exited during startup" >&2
    break
  fi
done
# Fallback: check logs
if [ $READY -ne 1 ]; then
  if grep -Ei "(Local URL|You can now view your Streamlit app|Server running on|Running on)" "$LOG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    READY=1
  fi
fi
if [ $READY -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "streamlit did not become ready within ${TOTAL_TIMEOUT}s" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$ST_PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 1; kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  exit 31
fi
# Run healthcheck
"$WS/healthcheck.sh" "$PORT" 10 3 || { echo 'healthcheck failed' >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true; PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$ST_PID" | tr -d ' ' || true); if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; exit 32; }
# Evidence
echo "validation: streamlit running PID=$ST_PID port=$PORT"
# Clean shutdown
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$ST_PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
  kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 2
  if ps -p "$ST_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
else
  kill -TERM "$ST_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
# Short log tail
tail -n 80 "$LOG" || true

Refined deps-01 to automatically detect pip-install wheel availability failures and attempt a safe requirements adjustment for numpy: if pip fails due to no matching distribution for a pinned numpy, the script queries pip index for the newest numpy wheel compatible with the running Python, replaces the pinned numpy in requirements.txt with that compatible version (preserving original in requirements.txt.bak), and retries installation. Also added a new small step: deps-01 now performs compatibility detection and automated pin relaxation for numpy only (keeps other pins intact). Updated change affects deps-01; other steps preserved (env-01, scaffold-01, test-01, validation-01). This addresses the CRITICAL blocking issue reported by the engineer by enabling an automated, auditable remediation path while remaining conservative and idempotent.
